statement: The province should require higher-density housing near transit stations, even where municipal zoning rules do not allow it.

passages.title: About David Eby
passages.quote: I cannot think of another premier out there who is that principled, and that steeped in the issues, with such a commitment to resolving them" - Megan Leslie, former Deputy leader of Canada’s NDP, co-founder of SALSA In his first eighteen months as Premier, David Eby has taken bold action for people. To tackle the housing crisis, he and our BC NDP team have brought in tough new rules regulating short-term rentals to turn them into homes for people, along with updating zoning rules province-wide to allow for more townhouses, duplexes and triplexes.

passages.title: (2024) A stronger BC working better for people: Speech from the Throne (BC NDP reprint)
passages.quote: Landmark changes made over the last year are helping to lay the foundation for a housing market that will work better for people. Turning short-term rentals, like Airbnbs, into long-term homes. Speeding up housing permit approvals. Fixing zoning rules that block construction of middle-class homes in existing neighbourhoods.

passages.title: (2024) A stronger BC working better for people: Speech from the Throne (BC NDP reprint)
passages.quote: Setting municipal targets for new housing construction. Getting more homes built near public transit. Building student housing at an unprecedented pace. And protecting affordable rentals from being turned into luxury condos by big real estate corporations.

passages.title: (2023) A BC where we all belong: Speech from the Throne (BC NDP reprint)
passages.quote: It is working with municipalities to set ambitious targets to deliver more housing where it is needed most. And it is breaking down permitting barriers that are preventing new homes from getting built quickly. In the months ahead, your government will make major new investments to increase housing and services near public transit hubs around the province. It will also launch a refreshed housing strategy.

passages.title: Results for You
passages.quote: Preliminary analysis indicates the BC could see about 100,000 extra homes near transit in the next ten years. We’ve invested $400 million to acquire and build on land near transit hubs. It’s not just about homes. It’s about an affordable home in a community you love.

passages.title: Results for You
passages.quote: Protected renters from bad faith evictions We’re supporting homeowners to provide more rental homes with easier and lower cost management, and protecting renters from being taken advantage of. Cut red tape and roadblocks We’ve fixed restrictive and outdated rules that were blocking townhouses, row homes and duplexes. Experts estimate the province could see more than 130,000 more small-scale multi-unit homes in BC over the next 10 years as a result of these changes. We also removed barriers to deliver more homes near transit hubs and other services, to make life easier where people live.

passages.title: B.C. NDP unveils election platform (2024), focusing on 'tough challenges' and John Rustad (iNFOnews)
passages.quote: The Conservatives have also released a series of pledges related to infrastructure, transit and boosting the economy, including Rustad’s promise to reintroduce a minister responsible for “red tape reduction.” “The key is we need to get to better management in this province. We need to be able to make sure that we unleash our potential,” he told reporters on Thursday. A statement from the Conservatives says they would eliminate B.C.’s nearly $9-billion deficit within two terms of government and require voter approval of any new taxes, through referendum or an election.

passages.title: (2024) A stronger BC working better for people: Speech from the Throne (BC NDP reprint)
passages.quote: People are facing big new challenges While BC’s economy is strong and growing, your government is nowhere near satisfied. Too many people are not feeling it yet. Too many are still struggling to get ahead. After decades where our housing market was allowed to serve the interests of investors and speculators, even those who earn a decent middle-class income are finding it hard to afford a home.

passages.title: Results for You
passages.quote: 1,500 homes have been protected since the fund was established in 2023, helping 2,500 people, with thousands more homes now under consideration for protection. Took the lead in new rental homes From 2018 to 2024, BC’s rental housing starts were 195.7% higher than from 2011 to 2017. 20.8% of all new rental homes being built in Canada are now being built in BC – our per capita rental housing starts are nearly 4x Ontario’s. Cut wait times for renters and landlords We’ve cut wait times at the Residential Tenancy Branch by almost 54% since 2022, by adding staff and making service improvements to provide resolutions faster.
